output.reason: The brief is convincing because it rests on specific comparisons that point at the tag stock rather than the handler: Pelion bags, loaded by the same Tessaly crews, show no rise, and old Brackwater tags read normally while Fennick tags failed at about 12% on the same days. It also gives clear steps (hold the breach notice, switch back to Brackwater stock, then test Fennick against printer settings), though it leaves open whether the stock is defective or the printers need a different heat setting.
